title: Kingdom of Singapura
capsule: The Kingdom of Singapura emerged around 1299 when the Srivijayan prince Sang Nila Utama (Sri Tri Buana) refounded the settlement of Temasek as Singapura — "Lion City" — at the southern tip of the Malay Peninsula, according to the Malay Annals. The polity grew into a significant entrepôt linking Malay Archipelago trade networks with routes to India and Yuan-dynasty China, with Fort Canning Hill serving as the royal compound; archaeological excavations there have confirmed a 14th-century settlement. The only historically well-attested ruler is Parameswara (later Iskandar Shah), who came to power around 1389 after fleeing Majapahit pressure. Around 1398–1402 the kingdom collapsed under Majapahit invasion, and Parameswara fled north to found the Malacca Sultanate, which became the dominant maritime power of 15th-century Southeast Asia.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is poorly attested; the kingdom's control is inferred largely from the Malay Annals and limited Fort Canning archaeology, with no surviving administrative records or precise boundary data.
